attribution.note: Marcus writes about himself in the third person in his own post. He is stating his own view.

semantics.note: Broadly faithful, but it drops the context. Marcus's point is that LLMs cannot check what they say against the world, so they produce plausible fabrications. 'Too dumb' is hyperbole about unreliability, not a claim of zero ability.

contract.note: The plain reading is stretched against the speaker. Support requires 'no meaningful discrimination' beyond chance. An informed reader would take the claim to mean LLMs cannot reliably tell truth from falsehood, especially in their own output. The contract flags this narrower reading but scores the extreme one, so modest above-chance accuracy refutes it.

evidence.note: Pre-post study of gpt-3.5-turbo classifying PolitiFact claims, at about 69% accuracy, above chance. This contradicts a claim of no ability. It does not show dependable verification.

Posted 2023-10-01, before the post. Most ChatGPT detectors showed no fact-verification ability on ChatGPT's own generations without tools. This supports the context-faithful reading that LLMs cannot check their own claims.

reviews.rationale: I marked the contract unfair: it scores an extreme 'no ability above chance' reading, which e1 refutes (about 69% binary accuracy). The ordinary reading in context is that LLMs cannot reliably separate fact from fabrication in what they generate, and e2 supports that (no verification ability on its own outputs). So the outcome is mixed: the strong reading fails, the reliability reading holds.
